es: Parafrasear un párrafo atribuyendo las ideas con verbos de cita adecuados (argue, claim, maintain, acknowledge, according to) y condensándolo con una nominalización.

teaching.en: To paraphrase a source, change the structure as well as the words, and keep the original meaning intact.
teaching.es: Para parafrasear una fuente, cambia la estructura además de las palabras y conserva intacto el significado original.
teaching.explanationEs: Cambiar dos o tres palabras no es parafrasear: hay que reorganizar la frase.
segments: To paraphrase a source, change the structure as well
as the words, and keep the original meaning intact.
teaching.audioText: To paraphrase a source, change the structure as well as the words, and keep the original meaning intact.

teaching.en: Copying a sentence verbatim and changing two words is not paraphrasing; it is copying with a small disguise.
teaching.es: Copiar una frase textualmente y cambiar dos palabras no es parafrasear; es copiar con un pequeño disfraz.
teaching.explanationEs: Verbatim significa «palabra por palabra»; si copias así, debes citar con comillas.
segments: Copying a sentence verbatim and changing two words is
not paraphrasing; it is copying with a small disguise.
teaching.audioText: Copying a sentence verbatim and changing two words is not paraphrasing; it is copying with a small disguise.

teaching.en: According to the survey, cycling has doubled: a reporting verb shows how far you agree with the source.
teaching.es: Según la encuesta, el ciclismo se ha duplicado: un verbo de cita muestra hasta qué punto estás de acuerdo con la fuente.
teaching.explanationEs: According to (con to) introduce una fuente neutral; el verbo de cita añade tu actitud.
segments: According to the survey, cycling has doubled: a reporting
verb shows how far you agree with the source.
teaching.audioText: According to the survey, cycling has doubled: a reporting verb shows how far you agree with the source.

teaching.en: Use claim to distance yourself from a statement that you doubt, and argue when you find the reasons persuasive.
teaching.es: Usa claim para distanciarte de una afirmación de la que dudas, y argue cuando las razones te parezcan convincentes.
teaching.explanationEs: Claim toma distancia; argue presenta una tesis defendida con razones.
segments: Use claim to distance yourself from a statement that you
doubt, and argue when you find the reasons persuasive.
teaching.audioText: Use claim to distance yourself from a statement that you doubt, and argue when you find the reasons persuasive.

teaching.en: Planners maintain that safer streets attract customers, and some economists contend that the investment pays for itself.
teaching.es: Los urbanistas sostienen que las calles más seguras atraen clientes, y algunos economistas afirman que la inversión se paga sola.
teaching.explanationEs: Maintain indica firmeza; contend es más formal, propio de textos académicos.
segments: Planners maintain that safer streets attract customers, and some
economists contend that the investment pays for itself.
teaching.audioText: Planners maintain that safer streets attract customers, and some economists contend that the investment pays for itself.

teaching.en: A careful writer will point out a weakness, acknowledge a limit or take issue with a doubtful claim, without attributing anything twice.
teaching.es: Un autor cuidadoso señalará una debilidad, reconocerá un límite o discrepará de una afirmación dudosa, sin atribuir nada dos veces.
teaching.explanationEs: Cada verbo de cita expresa una función: señalar, admitir o discrepar; una sola atribución por idea.
segments: A careful writer will point out a weakness, acknowledge a limit
or take issue with a doubtful claim, without attributing anything twice.
teaching.audioText: A careful writer will point out a weakness, acknowledge a limit or take issue with a doubtful claim, without attributing anything twice.

prompt.es: Quieres dejar claro que dudas de lo que afirma la fuente. ¿Qué frase eliges?

choices.text: Some commentators acknowledge that the lanes were cheap, yet the council's accounts suggest otherwise.
Some commentators claim that the lanes were cheap, yet the council's accounts suggest otherwise.
Some commentators maintain that the lanes were cheap, yet the council's accounts suggest otherwise.

feedback.es: Claim toma distancia de lo dicho; acknowledge admite que es verdad y maintain sugiere una convicción firme que tú no compartes.

hint.es: Busca el verbo que toma distancia de la afirmación.

origin.text: Source: An online post says that the new lanes were cheap to build, yet the council's own accounts show costs twice as high as planned.

prompt.es: Completa: «Según el segundo informe, el tráfico del centro ha bajado un nueve por ciento.»

feedback.es: Según se dice According to; sin to la atribución es incorrecta.

hint.es: Se escribe con mayúscula al empezar la frase.

origin.text: Two reports were published last week. ___ to the second, traffic in the centre has fallen by nine per cent.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los autores reconocen que su muestra era demasiado pequeña.»

answer.text: The authors acknowledge that their sample was too small

feedback.es: Acknowledge introduce un límite que los propios autores admiten, seguido de that + oración.

hint.es: El sujeto The authors va primero; that abre la oración subordinada.

prompt.es: Elige la paráfrasis que cambia la estructura y mantiene el sentido.

choices.text: Many more people began cycling after the city made new lanes, and this helped to cut down traffic in the centre of town.
According to the report, the growth in cycling led to the construction of the new lanes in the city.
According to the report, the new lanes led to a growth in cycling and a reduction in traffic in the centre.

feedback.es: Se atribuye la idea con According to y se nominaliza (growth, reduction); otra opción solo cambia palabras sueltas y otra invierte la causa.

origin.text: Original (from a city report): Many more people started cycling after the city built new lanes, and this helped to cut traffic in the centre.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué actitud muestra la hablante hacia lo que dicen los críticos.

choices.text: She doubts it and keeps her distance until fuller evidence is published.
She rejects it outright, since the shop owners have proved it wrong.
She accepts it as probable, although she would like more figures.

feedback.es: El verbo claim y la frase «treat that claim with care» muestran que la hablante duda y se distancia hasta ver los datos completos.

origin.audio: The critics claim that the lanes hurt local shops. The shop owners I spoke to say otherwise, and the figures, which are still partial, seem to support them. I would therefore treat that claim with care until someone publishes the full sales data.

prompt.es: Completa: «La investigadora señala que las ventas junto a los carriles han subido.»

feedback.es: Point out significa «hacer notar»; con she en presente necesita -s.

origin.text: The researcher ___ out that shops along the lanes have seen their sales grow, although she admits that her sample is small.

prompt.es: ¿Qué implica el uso de «claim» en este párrafo?

choices.text: That the writer accepts the figure but wants the council to publish it.
That the writer doubts the statement and will not accept it without evidence.
That the commentators are unreliable people whose opinions should be ignored entirely.
That the writer believes the council's accounts are false and were written to give readers a false picture.

feedback.es: Claim toma distancia, y el final («a hope rather than a forecast») confirma que el autor no acepta la cifra sin pruebas.

origin.text: Some commentators claim that the plan will pay for itself within five years. They may be right, but they do not say how they reached that figure, and the council's own accounts point the other way. Until someone explains the figure, I shall treat the claim as a hope rather than a forecast.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo matiza el planificador el dato de la investigadora.

choices.text: It was measured wrongly, because the data from outside the centre are limited.
It is only true of the city centre, where the authors collected their figures.
It looks bigger than it is, because it started from a very low base.

feedback.es: El planificador discrepa de esa cifra porque partía de una cifra muy baja; las otras opciones atribuyen al planificador lo que dice la autora principal.

origin.audio: The report notes that cycling has grown by two hundred per cent in five years. The lead author stresses that the growth is concentrated in the city centre, and she concedes that data from the areas outside the centre are very limited. A planner quoted in the same report takes issue with that figure: he says that the starting number was very low, so a large percentage does not mean a large number of people.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los autores reconocen que su encuesta fue limitada y piden una mayor.»

feedback.es: Acknowledge introduce una limitación admitida por los propios autores.

origin.text: The authors ___ that their survey was limited, and they ask the council to repeat it next year with a larger sample.

prompt.es: Parafrasea el informe en 100–140 palabras: dos verbos de cita y una nominalización.

answer.text: According to the council's study, the building of more than a hundred kilometres of new lanes for cyclists has been followed by a sharp growth in commuter cycling, from 3 to 11 per cent, and by a reduction in central traffic of nine per cent. Early opposition, especially from shopkeepers who feared losing customers to reduced parking, has proved wrong. The lead researcher argues that the scheme has already earned back its cost, since spending on road maintenance and health care has dropped, and she notes that shops beside the lanes now earn six per cent more. Some critics claim, however, that the findings for small firms cannot be trusted, because just forty of them replied. The researcher concedes that this is a weakness and recommends a second, larger survey next year, while the council, for its part, is considering further routes outside the centre but has not explained where the money will come from.
accepted: According to the council's study, the building of more than a hundred kilometres of new lanes for cyclists has been followed by a sharp growth in commuter cycling, from 3 to 11 per cent, and by a reduction in central traffic of nine per cent. Early opposition, especially from shopkeepers who feared losing customers to reduced parking, has proved wrong. The lead researcher argues that the scheme has already earned back its cost, since spending on road maintenance and health care has dropped, and she notes that shops beside the lanes now earn six per cent more. Some critics claim, however, that the findings for small firms cannot be trusted, because just forty of them replied. The researcher concedes that this is a weakness and recommends a second, larger survey next year, while the council, for its part, is considering further routes outside the centre but has not explained where the money will come from.

Since the council built its protected bike lanes, the published figures point to a rise in cycling to work and a fall in traffic, together with cleaner air. The lead researcher maintains that the project has already repaid its cost, noting lower spending on roads and health care and higher sales in shops beside the lanes. Some critics claim that the evidence on small businesses is unreliable, since few of them replied. She acknowledges that weakness and recommends a second, larger survey next year, while the council is already looking at further routes for cyclists.

Five years on, the study reports a growth in cycling and a decrease in central traffic, together with cleaner air and quieter streets. The lead researcher contends that the project has paid back its cost, because road repairs and health care now cost less, and she adds that shops beside the lanes are selling more. Critics claim that the findings on small shops cannot be trusted, since only forty of them replied. She admits this limit and suggests repeating the survey after a year with a wider sample, while the council is looking at further routes outside the centre.

feedback.es: Una buena paráfrasis cambia la estructura, atribuye cada idea una sola vez con verbos distintos, condensa con nominalizaciones y no copia frases del original.

origin.text: Five years ago, the city council decided to build more than one hundred kilometres of protected bike lanes. At first, many residents opposed the plan, and shop owners were especially worried, because they assumed that fewer parking places would mean fewer customers. However, the figures published this spring tell a different story. The proportion of people who cycle to work has risen from three per cent to eleven per cent, while car traffic in the centre has fallen by nine per cent. Air quality has improved, the main streets are quieter, and several schools report that more pupils now arrive by bicycle. The researcher who led the study argues that the investment has already paid for itself, because the city now spends less on road repairs and on health care. She points out that sales in the shops along the new lanes have grown by six per cent. Nevertheless, some critics claim that the results for small shops are unreliable, since only forty businesses answered the survey. The researcher acknowledges this limitation, and she suggests that the council should repeat the survey next year with a larger sample. Meanwhile, the council hopes to build more lanes in the north of the city, although it has not yet said who will pay for them.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere el autor sobre las preguntas de la encuesta que no se publican?

choices.text: That the council has lied on purpose about the survey results.
That the survey questions were too difficult for residents to answer.
That the survey is the only evidence that the council could have used.
That the results cannot be checked, so the council's argument deserves care.

feedback.es: Sin las preguntas no se puede verificar la encuesta: el autor invita a la cautela, pero no acusa al municipio de mentir.

origin.text: The council argues that the lanes are a success, but its figures come from its own survey, and it has not published the questions. Nobody outside the council can tell whether residents were asked fairly. It may be a good survey; it may not. Until the council shows its method, the claim rests on trust.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La investigadora señala un fallo pero mantiene su opinión.»

answer.text: The researcher points out a flaw but maintains her view

feedback.es: Points out señala el fallo y maintains her view mantiene la tesis; but une ambas ideas.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión de cita con su función en el texto.

feedback.es: Cada verbo cumple una función distinta: distanciarse, defender, admitir y discrepar.
